chunks: Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub narrated from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Isḥāq who said:

ʿAlī (peace be upon him) said: ‘I will surely tell you a ḥadīth that it behoves every believer to be aware of [and remember].’ He related it to us in the morning but we forgot it by nightfall. So we returned to him and said to him: ‘We have forgotten the ḥadīth you told us in the morning, and you had said that it behoves every believer to be aware of it, so please repeat it for us.’ So he said: ‘There is no Muslim who commits a sin and is then pardoned for it by Allah in this world, but that Allah is more majestic and noble than to punish him again for it in the Hereafter after having granted him respite in the world.’ Then he recited this verse: (And whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your own hands have committed, and He pardons much).

key_terms.يَعِيَهُ: to be aware of and remember

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of worldly afflictions as a form of divine pardon for sins?
ai.summary: Imam ʿAlī (peace be upon him) elucidates the principle of divine magnanimity, where Allah’s pardon of a sin through worldly affliction precludes a second punishment in the Hereafter, reflecting the concept of *ʿafw* (pardon) over *ʿadhab* (punishment). This narration, recorded in *Kitab al-Zuhd*, underscores the spiritual benefit of enduring trials as a means of expiation, aligning with Shia scholarly emphasis on the interplay between divine justice and mercy. The cited verse highlights that while retribution is just, Allah’s forgiveness often exceeds the scope of strict recompense.

en.shaykh-tahir-ridha-jaffer: 11.Al-Ḥasan ibn Maḥbūb narrated from Abū Ḥamzah, from Abū Isḥāq who said,

“ʿAlī (a) said, ‘I will surely tell you a ḥadīth that it behoves every believer to be aware of [and remember].’ He related it to us in the morning but we forgot it by nightfall. So we returned to him and said, ‘We have forgotten the ḥadīth you told us in the morning, and you had said that it behoves every believer to be aware of it, so please repeat it [for us].’ So he said, ‘There is no believer who commits a sin and is then pardoned for it by Allah in this world, but that Allah is more majestic and noble than to punish him again for it in the Hereafter after having [pardoned him and] granted him respite in the world.’ Then he recited the verse: Whatever affliction befalls you is because of what your own hands have committed, and He pardons much. (Q42:30).”
